comments.author: MrMcCall
comments.story: Why do some birds mimic the sounds of other species?
comments.why: Lyrebird imitating camera, car alarm and chainsaw
comments.text: Here's the one that blows my mind: [VIDEO] It's from one of (our honorary Uncle) David Attenborough's nature series, where a Lyre bird is imitating an analog professional camera, a car alarm, and a chainsaw. If I hadn't watched it well over a decade ago, I don't think I'd believe it. Search YT for 'lyre bird imitating chainsaw' for a choice of vids.

comments.author: Naracion
comments.story: Crows possess higher intelligence long thought a primarily human attribute
comments.why: Lyrebird imitating a chainsaw indistinguishably from the real thing
comments.text: You might enjoy the superb lyre bird imitating sounds as mind boggling as a chainsaw--and when I say imitate, I mean I couldn't have distinguished the lyre bird sound from a real chainsaw. It's really mind-boggling to me. [VIDEO]

comments.author: NamTaf
comments.story: A ‘viral’ new bird song in Canada is causing sparrows to change their tune
comments.text: The Lyrebird from Australia is probably the best at this. It can imitate just about anything - car alarms, other birdsongs, camera shutters, gunshots, etc. etc. [VIDEO] [LINK]
